rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 (kd 0.40, x = ±0.032 m, footprint 0.016 m, kp 3.0, ki 0.30, base_speed 1.5, last_direction) is the best raced design, scoring 372.74, up from 201.98. Oval finished 19 of 20 with max_error 0.042 and 0.25 line-loss events. Its steering oscillation (0.285) is above the 0.25 warning level, but finishes rose sharply, so the extra damping is working and I keep kd 0.40. The approved-input feedback (entityR1) is written against iteration 5 (kd 0.30, score 201.98). It treats that as the best design and asks me to test base_speed 1.3 only if kd 0.40 holds. That condition is met: oval finishes are 19 of 20, well above the 7 threshold, and the oscillation rise has not blocked completions. So the feedback's next step applies.

The remaining failures are the s-bend (progress 0.32, all 20 runs off track, max_error 0.062) and the slalom (progress 0.16, all 20 off track, max_error 0.064). Both are corner-entry or speed-limited failures. Neither has been tested against speed at this sensor spread.

Change: base_speed 1.5 to 1.3, a single-variable step. Everything else is held: kd 0.40, kp 3.0, ki 0.30, sensor x = ±0.032 m with antisymmetric weights (-1.6, -0.8, 0, 0.8, 1.6), footprint 0.016 m, mass 0.8 kg, and line_loss last_direction.

Expected result: lower speed reduces lateral drift and line losses on the s-bend and slalom, so their progress rises. Oval completion time rises from about 1.87 s to roughly 2.2 s, which still leaves margin under 3.0 s, so oval completions should hold near 19 of 20. The time term in the score falls slightly, so the net gain depends on how far the s-bend and slalom progress improves.

Risks: if the slalom needs more speed to clear its length, slowing could lower its progress, and the oval could still be fine but score less per time. Hypotheses: H1, the s-bend and slalom off-track events come from entering bends too fast, so 1.3 lets them complete more of the course. H2, oval finish time still has enough margin at 1.3. Measurements wanted: per-track progress, finish count, max_error location, line-loss timing (bend or straight), steering_oscillation, and completion_time on the oval.

Decision rule for next iteration: if s-bend or slalom progress rises and oval finishes stay at 19 or more, keep base_speed 1.3. If s-bend and slalom progress fall, or oval finishes drop below 15, return to base_speed 1.5 and test kp or kd 0.50 instead.
